introduce:
Lie down on your back, and put your hands beneath your hips for support. 

Then lift your legs up until they form a right angle with the floor. 

Slowly bring your legs back down and repeat the exercise.
name: LEG RAISES

tips.text: This workout should be done on a mat.
Raise up your legs faster and put them down slower.
Your back should always be flat on the floor.
Keep your legs as straight as possible.
Don't pull your shoulders up off the floor.
Exhale when lifting your legs, and inhale when lowering them.
If you feel it's too hard, put a little bend in your knees.
You shouldn't feel any pressure in your chest and shoulder area.
This exercise targets your lower abdominals.

introduce:
Lie on the floor with your toes and forearms on the ground. Keep your body straight and hold this position as long as you can. 

Don't hold your breath. Breathe normally from your abdomen instead of your chest.

This exercise strengthens the abdomen, back and shoulders.
name: PLANK

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your body straight.
Tighten your core and gluteus.
Don't sink or raise your hips.
Breathe naturally.
If you feel it's too easy, add weight on your lower back.
Too hard? Lower your knees on the mat with your ankles crossed in the air.
You should feel your abdominals burning, maybe even shivering.
It's not right if your shoulders or lower back are sore.
This exercise works your core.
This exercise is good for your spine.

introduce: Start in the push-up position. Bend your right knee towards your chest and keep your left leg straight, then quickly switch from one leg to the other. \n\nThis exercise strengthens multiple muscle groups.
name: MOUNTAIN CLIMBER

tips.text: We suggest you do this on a mat.
Bring your knees as close to your chest as possible.
Don't lift your hips up.
Take steady and deep breaths.
If you feel it's too easy, do it as fast as you can.
If you feel it's too hard, adjust to a speed that makes you feel comfortable.
If you feel it's too hard, elevate your hands on a bench.
This is a great full body exercise.
This can strengthen your cardiovascular system.

introduce:
Start in the push-up position, but keep your arms straight. 

Keep your body straight and hold this position as long as you can. 

Don't hold your breath. Breathe normally from your abdomen instead of your chest.

This exercise strengthens your abdomen and back muscles.
name: STRAIGHT-ARM PLANK

tips.text: This workout should be done on a mat.
Keep your body straight.
Put your hands directly underneath your shoulders.
Tighten your core and gluteus.
Do not sink your lower back or raise your hips in the air.
Breathe deeply.
Too easy for you? Add weight on your lower back.
You should feel your abdominals burning, maybe even shivering.
This exercise really works on your core and lower back.

introduce: Lie on your right side with your forearm supporting your body. Hold your body in a straight line. \n\nThis exercise targets the abdominal muscles and obliques.
name: SIDE PLANK RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your arm at a 90 degree angle.
Keep your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Open your chest.
Always keep your body straight.
Put pressure on your wrist and elbow.
Don't put pressure on your shoulders.
Breathe regularly.
To make it easier, put your top foot forward on the mat.
Your abdominals will be burning, maybe even shivering.
Your shoulder should not be sore.
This exercise can strengthen your core.

introduce: Lie on your left side with your forearm supporting your body. Hold your body in a straight line. \n\nThis exercise targets the abdominal muscles and obliques.
name: SIDE PLANK LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your arm at a 90 degree angle.
Keep your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Open your chest.
Always keep your body straight.
Put pressure on your wrist and elbow.
Don't put pressure on your shoulders.
Breathe regularly.
To make it easier, put your top foot forward on the mat.
Your abdominals will be burning, maybe even shivering.
Your shoulder should not be sore.
This exercise can strengthen your core.

introduce:
Lie on your back with arms at sides, palms down and legs extended. 

Lift your legs and cross the right thigh over the left, then reverse the exercise. 

Make sure your back is always flat.

It's a great exercise for the obliques and rectus abdominis.
name: SCISSORS

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your back flat on the floor.
Slightly bend your knees.
Breathe naturally.
To make it easier, place your hands under your glutes to get more balance.
This exercise primarily targets your lower abs.
This exercise can help you get great balance.

introduce: Lie on the ground with your legs bent and your arms by your sides. \n\nSlightly lift your upper body off the floor and make your hands alternately reach your heels.
name: HEEL TOUCH

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your neck in a natural position.
Keep your lower back on the floor.
Engage your core.
Exhale when touching your heels and inhale when going back.
It's a great exercise for all of your abdominal muscles.

introduce:
Stand on the floor with your arms extended to your sides at the shoulder height. 

Then bend your body and use your left hand to touch your right foot or get as close as you can. Switch sides and repeat.

Exhale when you bend your body and inhale when you come up. 

Keep your back and legs straight during the exercise.
name: CROSS TOUCH AND REACH

tips.text: Keep your back straight when bending your body.
Bend your body at 90 degrees.
Don't bend your knees.
Exhale as you bend down, and inhale as you come up.
When your arm is up in the air, you should feel stretch from your fingers to toes.
This exercise helps you warm up.
This exercise stretches your hamstrings, torso and arms.

introduce:
Start in the straight arm plank position. 

Then bend your right arm and place your forearm on the ground with your elbow under your shoulder, then bend your left arm and come down into the traditional plank position. 

Then reverse and come back to the start position. Repeat the exercise.

Keep your body straight during the exercise. Inhale when you come down and exhale when you come up.

It's a great exercise for the quadriceps, triceps and abdominal muscles.
name: UP AND DOWN PLANK

tips.text: Please do it on a mat.
Please keep your core tight.
Please keep your legs extended straight.
Please keep your head, neck and spine aligned.
Please don\'t sink or raise your hips.
Inhale deeply as you lower your body to help you lower further.
Exhale as you raise your body to help you keep stable.
This exercise strengthens and tones your core, arms, glutes, wrists and shoulders.

introduce: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. Bring your knee to your opposite elbow. \n\nReturn to the start position and repeat with the other side.
name: STANDING BICYCLE CRUNCHES

tips.text: Tighten your abdominals during the exercise.
Raise your knee up as high as you can.
Squeeze your abdominals with each crunch.
You can feel your entire core squeezing.
Exhale when lift your knees and inhale when lower them.
This exercise works on your entire core.

introduce:
Lie on your stomach with your legs straight and feet close together. Place your hands beneath your shoulders, and bend your elbows close to your body.

Inhale deeply, press your palms into the floor, lifting your chest and shoulders off the ground. Keep your hips pressed firmly into the floor. 

Hold for a few breaths, raise and lower with your breath. On inhale, lift into spinal extension. On exhale, soften the shoulders and deepen the stretch.
name: COBRA STRETCH

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Inhale to lift the chest. Exhale to soften the shoulders and deepen the stretch.
This exercise stretches your abdominals.
